# ChartBook

> A developer platform for data science teams to discover, document, and share analytics work. Provides a centralized catalog for pipelines, charts, and dataframes with automatic documentation website generation.

ChartBook organizes analytics work into **pipelines** (self-contained projects) or **catalogs** (multi-pipeline collections). All configuration uses TOML format (`chartbook.toml`).

## Installation

```bash
# For data loading
pip install chartbook

# For CLI (recommended: isolated installation)
pipx install chartbook
```

## Python API

```python
from chartbook import data

# Load dataframe (returns Polars LazyFrame by default) — bare pipeline name
lf = data.load(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data")

# Scoped pipeline name (canonical; required when a bare name is ambiguous)
lf = data.load(pipeline="acme/markets", dataframe="market_data")

# Load as Polars eager DataFrame
df = data.load(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data", format="polars_eager")

# Load as pandas DataFrame
df = data.load(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data", format="pandas")

# Explicit catalog path (no global config needed)
lf = data.load(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data",
               catalog_path="/path/to/catalog")

# Get resolved data file path
path = data.get_data_path(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data")

# Get documentation content as string
docs = data.get_docs(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data")

# Get path to documentation source file
docs_path = data.get_docs_path(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data")
```

## CLI Commands

```bash
chartbook build              # Generate HTML documentation
chartbook build -f           # Force overwrite existing docs
chartbook build --keep-build-dirs  # Keep temp files for debugging
chartbook publish            # Publish to directory
chartbook create-data-glimpses     # Create data summary report
chartbook config             # Configure default catalog path
```

## Global Configuration

User settings stored in `~/.chartbook/settings.toml`:

```toml
[catalog]
path = "/absolute/path/to/catalog/chartbook.toml"
```

Set via `chartbook config` command. When configured, `data.load()` works without explicit `catalog_path`.

## Project Types

The project type is inferred from structure: a manifest with a `[pipelines]` registry table is a **catalog**; otherwise it is a **pipeline**. An explicit `type = "pipeline"`/`"catalog"` in `[project]` is allowed; contradictions with the file structure are errors. There is no format version key. The minimal valid pipeline manifest is an empty file.

### Pipeline Project
```toml
[project]
name = "My Pipeline"     # Optional — defaults to the directory name
```

### Catalog Project (aggregates multiple pipelines)

Catalog keys are scoped pipeline IDs (`scope/name`), quoted because they contain `/`:

```toml
[project]
name = "My Catalog"

[pipelines."acme/sales"]
path = "../pipelines/sales"

[pipelines."acme/monthly"]
path = { unix = "/data/pipelines/monthly", windows = "T:/pipelines/monthly" }
```

## Configuration Reference

### [project] - Project Metadata (all keys optional)
```toml
[project]
name = "My Pipeline"                 # Default: directory name (doubles as site title)
description = "Description"
maintainer = "Your Name"             # Also rendered as site author
contributors = ["Name1", "Name2"]
repo_url = "https://..."             # Default: git remote origin
readme = "./README.md"               # Default
copyright = "2026"                   # Default: current year
logo = "./assets/logo.png"           # Default: bundled asset
favicon = "./assets/icon.png"        # Default: bundled asset
os_compatibility = ["Windows", "Linux"]
build = """
doit
"""                                  # Shell-script semantics (multi-line = one script)
site_dir = "./docs_src/site/"        # Default when that directory exists
# id = "myorg/my_pipeline"           # Scoped ID (default: derived from git remote + dirname)
```

### [charts.chart_id] - Chart Definitions
```toml
[charts.revenue_trend]
name = "Revenue Trend"
description = "Monthly revenue trends"
dataframe = "revenue_data"
path = "./_output/revenue_trend.html"
docs_path = "./docs_src/charts/revenue_trend.md"  # Or inline: docs = "..."
tags = ["Revenue", "Monthly"]                 # Optional
frequency = "Monthly"                         # Optional
units = "USD Millions"                        # Optional
date_cleared_by_iv_and_v = "2025-01-15"       # Optional: governance
last_legal_clearance_date = "2025-01-15"      # Optional: governance
```

Exactly one of `docs_path` (external markdown file) or `docs` (inline markdown) is required per chart.

### [dataframes.df_id] - Dataframe Definitions
```toml
[dataframes.market_data]
name = "Market Data"
description = "Daily stock prices"
sources = ["Bloomberg", "Reuters"]
path = "./_data/market_data.parquet"
date_col = "date"
docs_path = "./docs_src/dataframes/market_data.md"  # Or inline: docs = "..."
tags = ["Market Data", "Equities"]                  # Optional
providers = ["Bloomberg LP", "Refinitiv"]           # Optional
access_types = ["Subscription", "Subscription"]     # Optional
license = "Bloomberg Data License"                  # Optional
license_expiration = "2025-12-31"                   # Optional
```

Exactly one of `docs_path` or `docs` is required per dataframe.

### [notes] - Additional Documentation
```toml
[notes.methodology]
path = "./docs_src/methodology.md"
```

### [notebooks] - Jupyter Notebooks
The notebook name is inferred from the first `# Heading` in the notebook. Set `name` to override.
```toml
[notebooks.analysis]
description = "Initial data exploration"
path = "_output/analysis.ipynb"
```

## Directory Structure

```
my-pipeline/
├── chartbook.toml      # Configuration
├── _data/              # Parquet data files
├── _output/            # Generated HTML charts
├── docs_src/           # Markdown documentation
│   ├── charts/
│   ├── dataframes/
│   └── site/           # (Optional) Custom site pages (site_dir default)
└── src/                # Python source code
```
